headline: Q1/Q2 hardening: streaming, auth/transport, and tool-calling pipelines get systematic fixes
body:
Three parallel workstreams are landing this and next quarter, each addressing a cluster of reliability bugs rather than one-off patches.

Streaming (Q1, effort 8, no deps): we're fixing SSE parsing to tolerate proxied streams that omit the 'event:' field (the Bedrock-proxied Anthropic case), eliminating spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and restoring dropped response metadata/headers (e.g. x-request-id) during with_structured_output streaming, fixing the AttributeError crash in disable_streaming='tool_calling' (an AsyncStream is passed where a ChatCompletion is expected) and rescoping that flag to only disable streaming for tool-calling turns instead of globally, and routing agent/graph internal LLM calls through astream instead of ainvoke so on_llm_new_token actually fires end-to-end. There's also test-infra work: correcting a known-bad assertion in the core streaming error-callback suite, and establishing a release sequence that validates tool-call streaming (including for not-yet-supported providers like Mistral) before stricter langchain-tests are enforced. Worth flagging: the SSE-tolerance fix and the disable_streaming rescoping are both behavior changes — the former risks masking genuinely malformed responses from other providers, the latter changes semantics for anyone depending on the current (buggy) global-disable behavior.

Authentication (Q1, effort 8, no deps): ChatAnthropic gains support for custom HTTP clients with mTLS for corporate proxy/PKI setups. MCP tool discovery gets fixed to reliably forward auth headers/tokens (currently causing spurious 403s despite correct credentials). We're also consolidating AzureChatOpenAI and BaseChatOpenAI onto a shared httpx client/connection-pooling layer to remove redundant connection/auth setup — this refactor carries real regression risk since these integrations evolved independently. Separately, and flagged high-risk, we're closing an SSRF/allowlist bypass where environment-based auth checks let requests slip past host validation; scoping this carefully matters since it could break existing enterprise configs that rely on env-based auth to reach internal hosts.

Tool-calling (Q2, effort 8, no deps): this is the broadest of the three — provider-specific message validation (Gemini's thought-signature/turn-order rules) needs to accommodate injected precomputed tool-call history; malformed/fragmented streamed tool-call payloads need graceful degradation instead of crashes or silent wrong-tool execution; tool_choice should stop being forced to 'required' for reasoning models that only support 'auto'/'none'; ToolNode needs to reliably block execution of human-rejected tool calls (safety-critical — flagged high risk if edge cases remain unhandled); tool_call_id needs to be added to on_tool_start/on_tool_end for parallel-call observability; tool-call limits need a proactive warning before the hard cutoff; and handle_tool_error/ToolException handling needs to be unified across the @tool decorator, ToolNode, and wrap_tool_call middleware.
call_to_action: Review the HITL rejection-enforcement fix in the tool-calling theme and the SSRF/allowlist hardening in the authentication theme before implementation starts — both are flagged high-risk for incomplete edge-case coverage or breaking existing configs, and need sign-off on scoping.
